back: Traditional AI classifies, predicts or detects. Generative AI produces new content from a prompt.
A model trained on broad data before you ever see it. The default starting point.
Fine-tuning retrains with your examples and is expensive. Grounding supplies your data at request time and is usually the right first answer.
The billable units of text going in and coming out. Longer prompts, bigger context and longer answers all cost more.
The ROI case has to include usage, integration and oversight — not the licence price alone.
Fabrications, inconsistent reliability and inherited bias are properties of the technology, not defects awaiting a patch.
Stating role, format, constraints and an example measurably improves output.
Connecting a model to your own content so answers are specific and citable.
Retrieve the relevant passages first, then answer from them. Current and citable without retraining.
Drafting in Word, analysing in Excel, summarising threads in Outlook, recapping in Teams.
The layer that grounds licensed Copilot in your organisation's own data, making answers business-specific.
Start from the app the work already happens in, not from the technology.
The agent for multi-step investigation across many sources.
The agent for reasoning over data to produce figures and charts.
Extend the existing Copilot when the gap is knowledge; build in Copilot Studio when the gap is behaviour.
The pro-code end: a model catalogue, Azure AI Search for retrieval, plus vision and language capabilities.
The retrieval service behind grounded answers over your own indexed content.
A trade-off of capability, latency and cost. The right answer is the smallest model that reliably does the job.
Fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, accountability.
Turning principles into owned decisions: which use cases are approved, what review they need, and who can say no.
A cross-functional body with real authority over AI strategy and oversight.
The group that owns the rollout itself, distinct from the council that sets policy.
No clear use case, no visible sponsorship, fear about job security, and no time set aside to learn.
Spreading capability peer to peer, which works because the person showing you a prompt sits next to you.
Included with some subscriptions, purchased monthly per user, or consumed pay-as-you-go.
Consumption-based, with commitment tiers where volume is predictable.
Depends on how steady and concentrated usage is, and whether committing buys a better rate.
